title: 2002 Tampa Plane Crash
summary: On January 5, 2002, 15-year-old Charles J. Bishop stole a Cessna 172 light aircraft from East Lake High School after being left alone for a preflight inspection. Without permission, he started the engine and took off from Tarpon Springs, Florida, despite immediate alerts from air traffic control and repeated warnings from a U.S. Coast Guard helicopter. Inspired by the September 11 attacks and motivated by anti-American sentiment, Bishop deliberately flew the aircraft into the Bank of America Tower in downtown Tampa, impacting between the 28th and 29th floors. The crash killed only Bishop and damaged one office room with no other injuries. Investigators ruled out terrorism connections and concluded the act was suicide, possibly influenced by psychological side effects of the acne medication Accutane.

The crew successfully ditched in the shallow Bengawan Solo River with the fuselage and wings largely intact. One flight attendant died during evacuation.

title: Air China 129
summary: Boeing 767 crashed into Mount Dotdae near Gimhae Airport during a circling approach to runway 18R. The crew exercised poor crew resource management and lost situational awareness during the approach, flying outside the circling approach area and delaying the base turn. The aircraft was not equipped with terrain warning systems suited for circling approaches, and the crew had never trained for a circling approach to this airport in the airline's simulator. When the first officer advised the captain to execute a missed approach about five seconds before impact, the captain did not respond.
probable_cause: The crew exercised poor crew resource management and lost situational awareness during the circling approach, flying outside the circling approach area and delaying the base turn. The crew did not execute a missed approach when visual contact with the runway was lost. Contributing factors included lack of training for this specific circling approach, disabled ATC ground surveillance systems, and inadequate awareness of weather minimums for the aircraft type.

title: EgyptAir 843
summary: EgyptAir Flight 843, a Boeing 737-566, departed Cairo on 7 May 2002 for Tunis. On approach to runway 11 in instrument meteorological conditions with fog, rain and blowing sand, the aircraft descended below safe altitude. The aircraft crashed on a hill in the Nahli area, 4 miles from the airport at an elevation of 750 feet. Investigation found the Minimum Safe Altitude Warning device at Tunis-Carthage did not cover the approach to runway 11.

title: China Airlines 611

location.name: Taiwan Strait, 26 miles northeast of Penghu Islands

summary: China Airlines Flight 611 disintegrated in mid-air during climb on May 25, 2002, 20 minutes after takeoff from Taiwan. The in-flight breakup was caused by structural failure from metal fatigue cracks in the vertical stabilizer spar that had originated from an improper repair following a tail strike 22 years earlier at Kai Tak Airport in 1980. The aircraft had accumulated over 64,800 flight hours, and fatigue from repeated pressurization cycles caused tiny cracks to propagate until catastrophic failure occurred.
probable_cause: Metal fatigue cracking from an unapproved repair procedure performed after a tail strike in 1980, where a doubler plate was installed over damaged skin contrary to Boeing structural repair manual requirements, leading to structural failure during climb.

Hidden cracks beneath the doubler plate were not detected during maintenance inspections over 22 years of service.

title: 2002 airtanker crashes
summary: On 17 June 2002, Lockheed C-130A Hercules (Tanker 130, N130HP) operated by Hawkins & Powers Aviation was performing aerial firefighting operations for the Cannon Fire near Walker, California. title: 2002 Bristow Helicopters Sikorsky S-76A crash
summary: A 22-year-old Sikorsky S-76A helicopter on a ten-minute flight between oil platforms experienced a main rotor blade failure during cruise. title: Northwest Airlines 85
summary: Northwest Airlines Flight 85 experienced a lower rudder hardover at FL350 when the rudder suddenly deflected to its full left limit. The crew successfully managed the asymmetric control deflection using ailerons and asymmetric engine thrust, diverting to Anchorage. A fatigue crack in the rudder power control module housing caused the failure. The aircraft had been in continuous service since 1989, and fatigue cracks were not visually detectable.
probable_cause: Fatigue fracture of the lower rudder power control module manifold resulted in a lower rudder hardover. The cast metal housing had broken, and the end portion housing the yaw damper actuator separated from the main portion. The failure mode was unusual because most similar failures involve internal components rather than the housing itself.

title: TransAsia Airways 791
summary: TransAsia Airways Flight 791, an ATR 72-200 freighter, departed Taoyuan at 1:04 am on 21 December 2002 bound for Macau. At 1:51 am while at flight level 180, the crew requested descent to FL160. The aircraft rapidly descended and disappeared from radar at 1:52 am, 17 km southwest of Magong. The crew detected severe icing conditions and activated the anti-ice system multiple times starting at 1:34 am. The stick shaker activated followed by stall warning. The autopilot was disengaged but recovery failed and the aircraft crashed into the sea. Both crew members were killed.
probable_cause: The crew encountered severe icing conditions beyond the ATR 72's certification envelope. Despite detecting icing and activating the anti-ice system, the flight crew lacked situational awareness and did not respond with appropriate action. The crew did not change altitude immediately nor follow severe icing emergency procedures. The aircraft entered an aerodynamic stall from which recovery failed.

title: Aeromist-Kharkiv 2137
summary: Aeromist-Kharkiv Flight 2137, an Antonov An-140, crashed into high ground near Ardestan, Iran during a night-time descent to Isfahan International Airport. The crew made procedural navigation errors, including incorrect use of GPS satellite navigation, failure to apply standard approach procedures, and poor crew management. The aircraft struck terrain and all 44 aboard were killed.
probable_cause: The primary cause was procedural navigation errors by the crew, including incorrect GPS use, failure to apply approach procedures, and failure to use other available navigation equipment. The crew did not seek an alternative approach when they realized GPS was not providing reliable distance information.
